newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters welcomes downtrend in inflation data.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters welcomes downtrend in inflation data.

text.p: New Zealand's Deputy Prime Minister and Treasurer Winston Peters on Tuesday welcomed March quarter inflation data which he said supported expectations of a downward trend in inflationary pressures.
"I am pleased to see that inflation continues to move towards the middle of the zero to three percent Reserve Bank target," he said in a statement.
"This latest figure is in line with the trend of Reserve Bank projections for falling inflationary pressures," Peters added.
Data from the government statistics office earlier today showed that consumer prices fell in the March quarter by 0.3 percent, while they rose by 1.8 percent on an annual basis.
Peters called the quarter-on-quarter fall "the first quarterly decrease since December 1991 and the largest quarterly decline since March 1961".

Reserve Bank of New Zealand calculations released during the morning showed the underlying inflation rate fell to 2.0 percent for the year to March. This compared with an underlying annual rate of 2.4 percent in the quarter to December.
